chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad reported to me, from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham, from Murazim, from al-Sadiq Ja’far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said:

"What has happened to some people of my Ummah? When Ibrahim and the progeny of Ibrahim are mentioned before them, their hearts become cheerful and their faces beam with joy; but when I and my Ahlul Bayt are mentioned, their hearts become averse and their faces frown!

By the One Who sent me as a truthful Prophet, even if a man were to meet God with the deeds of seventy prophets, but did not come with the authority (wilayah) of those in command from among us, the Ahlul Bayt, God would not accept from him any obligatory or voluntary act of worship."

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahlul Bayt - the People of the House, referring to the Prophet’s family
key_terms.أولي الأمر: Uli al-Amr - those vested with authority, interpreted in Shia tradition as the Imams from the Ahlul Bayt
key_terms.صرفا ولا عدلا: Obligatory and voluntary acts - the two categories of worship in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.ولاية: Wilayah - spiritual and temporal authority/guardianship of the Ahlul Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about accepting deeds without love for Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) criticizes those in his Ummah who celebrate the mention of Prophet Ibrahim and his family but show aversion when the Prophet and his Ahlul Bayt are mentioned. He then makes a powerful oath that even the deeds of seventy prophets would not be accepted by God without adherence to the wilayah (authority) of the Ahlul Bayt. This hadith, narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), underscores the centrality of wilayah in Shia doctrine and was addressed to the early Muslim community where competing loyalties and factions were already forming.
